records.excerpt: Imagine taking a coloured square between your fingers and drawing it towards your wrist. Suppose we let its neighbours follow, still joined, bending as you pull. A corner folds around your arm; the rest trails across the floor. We have not built this behaviour. Some draws might choose which squares come loose. Keeping them connected would require another rule.
records.proposition: A coloured grid can acquire relations that allow part of it to be worn; this is an interpretation of the passage, not installed behaviour.

records.excerpt: Perhaps particles are allowed to establish permanent connections. Perhaps a boundary remembers previous collisions and gradually becomes permeable. Perhaps the field governing their motion is modified by the traces they leave behind.
records.proposition: A boundary can retain contact history and change what it admits.
